summary: A 1939 steel H-beam lookout tower on Sierra National Forest, built on a site used since 1912, now deteriorating and repurposed as a communications tower.

facts.design: 20-foot H-beam steel tower with C-3(L) cab (1939); originally a compass-type station (1912), rebuilt as a cab/cabin tower (1924)
facts.status_note: Not maintained as a lookout; deteriorating; now used as a communications tower

access.note: No source found describes current public access, closure, or permission requirements; site now functions as a communications facility

visit.trail_note: No source found gives drive/trail access details

events.note: Replaced with a cab/cabin type tower, non-continuous staffing
Replaced with current 20-foot H-Beam Steel Tower with C-3(L) cab
Added to National Historic Lookout Register as US 1315, CA 138, on October 19, 2019

evidence.quote: The lookout was originally constructed in 1912 and was a compass type lookout.

evidence.supports: Replaced 1924 with cab/cabin tower, non-continuous staffing
evidence.quote: It was replaced in 1924 with a cab/cabin type of tower and was non-continuous staffing.

evidence.supports: Replaced 1939 with current 20-foot H-Beam Steel Tower and C-3(L) cab
evidence.quote: In 1939 it was replaced with the current type of tower, 20 foot, H-Beam Steel Tower with a C-3(L)Cab.

evidence.supports: Not maintained, deteriorating, used as communications tower
evidence.quote: The tower has not been maintained and has been deteriorating over the years. It is now used as a communications tower.

notes_for_editor: The two sources are near-duplicates (NHLR cites fire-lookouts.org as its source), so this is effectively a single-source history. No information found on current public access, a rental program, or precise staffing end date. The brief's event list matched these two sources exactly; no corrections needed. Worth a follow-up check with Sierra National Forest or Forest Fire Lookout Association for current access/condition details.
